subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Cup of Excellence Auctions
description: A quick win: understand Cup of Excellence Auctions.

hook.text: Cup of Excellence is a competition where the best coffees in a country are auctioned online to global buyers.

buildup.text: Winning lots are bid on by roasters worldwide. Prices often reach 10–50x the commodity market rate.

discovery.text: A 2023 Ethiopian lot sold for over $150 per pound—compared to the C-price of roughly $1.70. The premium is staggering.

twist.text: All auction money goes directly to the farmer. No middlemen take a cut from the winning bid.

climax.text: Winning transforms a farmer's life overnight—funding new equipment, education, and community improvement.

punchline.text: Grow the best coffee, win the auction, change everything.

quiz.question: What happens to auction money from Cup of Excellence?
options: It goes directly to the farmer

details.summary: The Cup of Excellence is an annual competition held in producing countries where coffees are blind-cupped by international judges. Winners are sold at online auction, often reaching prices of 50 to over 300 dollars per pound. It puts exceptional micro-lots on the global specialty map.
details.whyItMatters: Cup of Excellence proves that exceptional quality commands extraordinary prices, giving farmers a direct incentive to pursue excellence and validating specialty coffee as a premium category.
takeaways: Winning coffees sell for 50 to 300+ dollars per pound
Competitions are judged blind by international cupping panels
Auctions connect exceptional farmers directly with global buyers

faq.question: How does the Cup of Excellence competition work?
faq.answer: Farmers submit their best lots. National and international judges blind-cup hundreds of entries over multiple rounds. The top-scoring coffees are auctioned online to roasters worldwide. Winning farmers receive the full auction price minus a small administrative fee.

faq.question: Why do roasters pay hundreds of dollars per pound?
faq.answer: These are exceptionally rare coffees representing the pinnacle of quality. Roasters purchase them for prestige, to offer unique limited releases, and to build direct relationships with top producers. The quantities are tiny, often just a few hundred pounds.
